title: Toolchain Lite onramp - personal scratchpad
body:
Goal / hypothesis:
- Build a "Toolchain Lite" experience that lets product teams get a working Redwood inference pipeline (text gen / chat) into a prototype within 30 minutes with zero infra setup.
- Hypothesis: reducing friction for product experiments increases usage and surfaces more Hosted API conversions.

Problem statement:
- Current quickstarts are too dev-heavy: SDK install + API keys + environment config + prompt plumbing. For PMs/designers/early-POCs we should have a friction-free flow.
- UX gaps: lack of prebuilt connectors (Figma, Airtable, Notion, Slack), limited demo data mapping, no turnkey prompt templates for common patterns (summarization, Q&A, assistant).

Target users / personas:
- PM building proof-of-concept chat for internal demo (non-engineer or only a single eng partner).
- Solutions engineer who needs to prototype a customer workflow quickly to validate feasibility.
- Designer / researcher testing conversational UI patterns with sample data.

Core idea (rough):
- A lightweight web flow (hosted in Console) titled "Toolchain Lite" that guides users through:
  1) Choose use case (summarize docs, chat assistant, email draft, knowledge base Q&A).
  2) Pick a connector or upload sample data (Notion export / CSV / paste / Slack thread).
  3) Select a prompt template and persona (assistant, tutor, summarizer) with editable fields.
  4) Run a live preview (sample conversation) and iterate.
  5) Generate a small embed/embed+endpoint snippet to drop into a prototype (Web embed + prefilled config).
- Behind the scenes: we provision a temporary, ephemeral API key scoped to the user with strict quotas and telemetry for conversion signals.

Key features (MVP list):
- Templates: 8-10 curated prompt templates + example datasets.
- Connectors: CSV paste, Notion importer, Slack thread importer, Google Docs paste.
- Web preview: live chat UI with streaming responses and token cost estimate.
- One-click prototype export: snippet (vanilla JS) + prepopulated prompt + ephemeral key.
- Safety / quotas: per-session rate limit, per-user token cap, explicit data residency notice.

User stories (rough):
- As a PM, I can import a Notion doc and get a 3-sentence summary so I can show stakeholders the idea quickly.
- As a designer, I can select an assistant persona and run sample chats so I can test the tone in prototype flows.
- As an SE, I can export a JS snippet and hand it to my front-end to drop into an internal demo (no infra work).
- As a micro-sales rep, I can create a customer-specific sample (CSV of product docs) and send a link to demo the assistant.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- End-to-end flow from data import to prototype snippet in <30 mins for first-time user with no SDK knowledge.
- Preview supports streaming and shows tokens/cost estimate for the preview run.
- Exported snippet can be embedded in a static HTML page and works without any additional backend setup for demo scale.
- Telemetry captures: time-to-first-preview, template used, connector used, sample token usage.

Metrics to measure success:
- Time-to-first-preview (median) — target <12 minutes in first 90 days.
- Conversion: percent of Toolchain Lite sessions that lead to API key creation or signup upgrade within 30 days.
- Engagement: average number of previews per session.
- Feedback: collection of qualitative notes via in-flow survey (one question).

Risks & guardrails:
- Data leakage from uploaded customer files — must add clear data handling and expiration (auto-delete sample after X days) and a visible discloser.
- Abuse — ephemeral keys and low default quotas; detect high-volume automated use and require upgrade.
- Misaligned expectations — make the product boundaries explicit (prototype only, not production grade).

Operational considerations:
- Ephemeral key implementation: Console creates a scoped key via platform API with TTL (72 hours) and limited token budget.
- Billing signal: attribute token consumption to a "sandbox" internal bucket until user upgrades; track owner for conversion attribution.
- Instrumentation: events for connector chosen, template variant, export clicked, upgrade clicked.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Which templates to ship first? Suggest shortlist: meeting notes summarizer, knowledge base Q&A (context window aware), email composer, user interview summarizer, product feature explainer.
- How to present cost estimates without scaring non-technical users? Idea: show relative categories (tiny / small / medium) + approximate $ per 1K tokens.
- Data retention policy for uploaded samples (default delete after 7 days?) — check legal.
- Should exported snippet include a client-side key (risk) or always proxy through a hosted sandbox endpoint? Tradeoffs: ease vs security.

Experiment ideas (quick wins):
- Launch an internal beta in a single GTM pod; measure session conversions and qualitative feedback.
- Run A/B: show token estimate vs hide token estimate to see impact on completion rate.
- Preload demo templates for target industries: e-comm product Q&A, HR onboarding assistant, support ticket summarizer.

Implementation sketch (engineering notes):
- Frontend: small React flow reusing existing Console components for auth/layout.
- Backend: new "sandbox" service that issues ephemeral keys, enforces quotas, and proxies requests to hosted inference.
- Connectors: lightweight parsers (CSV -> docs, Notion export -> docs, Slack thread -> chunked docs). Use existing ingestion library where possible.
- Security: default to regional endpoints matching user's locale + explicit popup for uploads.

Next steps (what I want to do in the next 2 weeks):
- Draft a short mockup of the flow (2 screens: import + preview) and get 1rd with PM and 1 SE.
- Validate legal on sample retention and ephemeral key wording.
- Build a tiny hack prototype (frontend + ephemeral key) for internal demo.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could we pair this with a "guided transcript" feature so users can feed meeting recordings and get highlights? Might be a paid connector.
- Consider a "shareable demo link" that expires and counts as an outbound product touch for sales.
- If adoption is high, funnel templates into a marketplace (curated by solutions eng).

Links / references to check before next pass:
- Confluence draft: confluence:INFRON-4574 (ephemeral-keys design)
- Prior notebook: users/prompt-provenance-lineage-idea-log.json (seen in drive)
- Slack thread: #devexp-onboarding for past convo about snippets

Small checklist before sending to PM for feedback:
- [ ] Mockups attached
- [ ] Legal OK on retention language
- [ ] Prototype demo running internally
- [ ] Simple analytics dashboard for tool conversions

End.
